note: smart_sql_idmap ships exactly one migrate id_map plugin (id 'smart_sql', class SmartSql extends core Sql), opted into per migration with idMap: {plugin: smart_sql}. It has no config object, no schema, no services, no permissions, no admin UI. This site's migration PLUGIN MANAGER discovery is broken by pathauto, so medium/hard cases are grounded in the id_map plugin definition and in migrate_plus.migration.* CONFIG ENTITIES (created/read/deleted via entity storage), NOT in live migration executions. The id_map manager (plugin.manager.migrate.id_map) does list smart_sql, and migrate_plus migration config entities carry the idMap key that the plugin id is read from.

evals.prompt: I have a Drupal migration whose plugin ID is very long. How do I make it use the Smart SQL ID Map module's id map instead of core's default? Show exactly what to add to the migration definition.
evals.expected_output: Add an idMap key to the migration definition: idMap:\n  plugin: smart_sql . Works the same in a code migration YAML and in a migrate_plus.migration config entity; source/process/destination are unchanged.

evals.prompt: What core Drupal migrate problem does the smart_sql_idmap module work around, and why does it matter for migrations with long plugin IDs?
evals.expected_output: Core derives map/message table names and truncates them to MySQL's 63-character identifier limit, so two long-id migrations can collapse to the same table name and corrupt id lookups (issue #2845340). smart_sql computes shorter, md5-suffixed, collision-free table names; it also fixes getRowByDestination()/rollback (#3227549, #3227660).

evals.prompt: In the smart_sql_idmap module, what kind of migrate plugin is provided and what is its plugin ID and class?
evals.expected_output: It provides a migrate id_map plugin with id 'smart_sql' (annotation @PluginID("smart_sql")), class Drupal\smart_sql_idmap\Plugin\migrate\id_map\SmartSql, which extends core's id_map\Sql plugin.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a migration configuration named ssi_known (a migrate_plus.migration config entity). Inspect the running site and state which migrate id map (idMap) plugin that migration is configured to use.
evals.expected_output: ssi_known uses idMap.plugin: smart_sql (read via `drush config:get migrate_plus.migration.ssi_known idMap`).

evals.prompt: This site has two migration configurations, ssi_plain and ssi_smart. Exactly one of them is configured to use the smart_sql_idmap module's id map. Inspect the live configuration and state which migration uses the smart_sql id map plugin.
evals.expected_output: ssi_smart uses idMap.plugin: smart_sql; ssi_plain uses idMap.plugin: sql (core). Check `drush config:get migrate_plus.migration.ssi_smart idMap` and the same for ssi_plain.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a migrate_plus migration configuration entity with the id ssi_task that uses the Smart SQL ID Map module's id map plugin. A minimal migration is fine (e.g. source plugin embedded_data with an integer id, empty process, destination plugin null) but it MUST be configured to use the smart_sql id map. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A migration config entity migrate_plus.migration.ssi_task exists with idMap: { plugin: smart_sql }. Create it via the migration entity storage or config import.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is an existing migration configuration ssi_switch that currently uses core's default sql id map. Reconfigure it so it uses the smart_sql_idmap module's id map plugin instead, and apply the change to the live site. Do not change its source, process, or destination.
evals.expected_output: migrate_plus.migration.ssi_switch now has idMap.plugin: smart_sql (was sql).
